Septoplasty and turbinate reduction

The septum is the wall between the two sides of the nose, and a deviated septum is one of the commonest causes of chronic blockage. Septoplasty straightens it from inside the nose, and is often combined with reduction of enlarged turbinates to open the airway.

At a glance

Operating time
About 45 to 90 minutes
Anaesthesia
General
Incisions
Inside the nose only
Back to work
Usually after about a week
Book a consultation

Symptoms that may point to a deviated septum

  • persistent blockage on one or both sides
  • mouth breathing, especially during sleep
  • snoring or disturbed sleep
  • recurrent nosebleeds
  • recurrent sinus infections or mid-facial pressure in some patients

Not every blockage is caused by the septum; allergy, enlarged turbinates and polyps are also common causes, which is why treatment starts with an accurate diagnosis.

Diagnosis

Examination includes nasal endoscopy in clinic to assess the septum, turbinates and nasal valves. A CT scan may be requested if a sinus problem is suspected, and medical treatment is tried first where appropriate.

How is it done?

The operation is performed entirely through the nostrils. The deviated part of the cartilage or bone is reshaped and repositioned to the midline, and the outside of the nose is unchanged. Enlarged turbinates are reduced with techniques that preserve their lining and function.

Recovery

Congestion is most noticeable in the first one to two weeks, and saline rinses are recommended. Most patients return to work within about a week, and breathing improves progressively as internal swelling settles over the following weeks.

Frequently asked questions

Will septoplasty change the shape of my nose?

No. It is done from the inside and does not change the external shape. If you also want a change in shape, it can be combined with rhinoplasty in one operation.

Is it covered by insurance?

As a functional procedure it may be covered, depending on your policy and documented diagnosis. This is checked before scheduling.

Will my nose be packed?

It depends on the case. Often thin internal splints or no packing at all are used, and splints are removed in clinic after a few days.

Will it cure my snoring?

It may improve snoring related to nasal blockage, but snoring has other causes in the throat. If sleep apnoea is suspected, further assessment may be needed.
